title: Labels that match their sources
statement: Make every source's label, which work, by whom, where, when and what kind of document, match the source text, in generated items and in the source bank.
example: An audit of one bank of real sources found 198 of 436 era tags wrong.
detail: AP judges failed generated items whose document labels contradicted their content: one document was labelled a manuscript illustration but described as a map, and others carried primary-source titles and dates their text did not match (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/research/failure_taxonomy.md`). An audit of the project's bank of real source documents caught 198 of 436 era tags wrong and 4 catalogue entries that pointed to a different work from the one named, errors that would have baked fabrication into the next model's training, and audit gates became mandatory before the next stage (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/MEMORY.md`). Check each label against the source text as a claim of its own, and audit the source bank before anything is built from it. Generated source sets fail more on attribution than on their sentences.
against: The bank audit was an agent's audit of a training corpus with spot checks, not a full review by a person, and the two judge rationales are single items. Dropping attributions trades one score for another: the variant without them had the best factual accuracy (70%), but the best pass rate (60%) came from the one that also added curriculum facts (`sft_v4_prompt_engineering.md`, line 16). The attribution fixes for document-based items were never re-measured (`findings_sftv7_20260424.md`, line 138).
